This dish featured long, thin pasta noodles served with a creamy cheese sauce, similar to what we have today.

The recipe for macaroni and cheese was brought to the United States by English settlers in the 17th century. At the time, the dish was known as "macaroni pie" because it was often topped with an egg custard similar to a piecrust. Over time, the recipe evolved and the top was removed from the pie, making it more like the mac and cheese we enjoy today.

In the 20th century, mac and cheese became a staple of American comfort food. It was a popular dish in school cafeterias and restaurants, and its creamy, cheesy flavors made it a crowd-pleaser. Today, mac and cheese is enjoyed all over the world and comes in many different variations, from simple mac and cheese to loaded mac and cheese, which contains extra toppings like bacon, cheese, and vegetables.
